Agreement on phylogenetic signal findings (C14-C17, C42-C44). Both evaluations support the parafit test results showing phylogenetic structure. Perfect agreement on linear model results for network structure (C18-C19, C47-C48, C54). Both evaluations find the statistical methodology sound and results well-supported. Peer reviewers praise the 'solid set of analyses' without raising methodological concerns.

Agreement on statistical results (C20, C58-C59), though OpenEval notes the mechanistic interpretation (dilution effects) remains speculative. Peer reviewers accept the finding without raising concerns about the interpretation of this unexpected result.

Agreement on canopy cover effects (C21-C22, C65). Both evaluations find the negative relationships well-supported by linear models. OpenEval highlights supporting citations for microclimate effects, while peer reviewers acknowledge these findings without concerns.

Agreement on non-significant results for parasitoid generality (C23-C24, C53). Both evaluations appropriately accept null results. OpenEval commends proper reporting of non-significant findings, while peer reviewers accept this as part of the comprehensive analytical approach.

Agreement on null model results (C28-C30). Both evaluations support the methodology and conclusions about non-random assembly. OpenEval details the Patefield approach with 10,000 simulations, while peer reviewers acknowledge the 'solid set of analyses.'

Agreement on main synthesis and conclusions (C31-C33, C107-C110). Both evaluations find the summary claims well-supported by collective evidence. Peer reviewers describe the study as 'valuable' with 'solid evidence,' while OpenEval confirms conclusions integrate results appropriately.

Disagreement on temporal pooling methodology (C93). OpenEval finds the statistical methodology comprehensive and appropriate, rating it SUPPORTED.
